paragraphs: Reinforcement learning agents can struggle when their surroundings change. Unsupervised environment design addresses this by generating training environments suited to an agent’s current abilities. The paper identifies the environment generator as an important bottleneck: even a useful training strategy depends on being able to produce varied situations that help the agent improve.

The proposed method, ADD, uses a diffusion model to generate environments and guides that generator with the agent’s regret. This guidance aims to produce situations that are challenging while still offering opportunities for improvement. The diffusion model supplies the expressive capacity to generate adversarial environments while preserving diversity across the training experience.

In the reported experiments, ADD produces a useful curriculum and outperforms other environment-design methods when agents face unfamiliar environments without further training. These results support the idea that choosing training challenges and maintaining their variety can work together. The finding concerns the tested out-of-distribution environments; it demonstrates improved generalization there rather than establishing robustness to every possible environmental change.
neurips-2024-adversarial-environment-des.tldr: ADD uses regret-guided diffusion to generate diverse training challenges and improves agents’ generalization to unfamiliar environments in experiments.

paragraphs: Structured pruning reduces a neural network by removing entire components, such as neurons or convolutional filters, that have little effect on its output. This can improve computational and energy efficiency while preserving useful predictive performance. The paper introduces BMRS, an end-to-end Bayesian approach for deciding which structures to remove.

BMRS combines structured pruning through multiplicative noise with Bayesian model reduction. The latter provides an efficient way to compare Bayesian models when their prior assumptions change. The authors derive two versions with different pruning behavior. BMRS_N uses a truncated log-normal prior and offers reliable compression and accuracy without requiring a pruning threshold to be tuned. BMRS_U uses a truncated log-uniform prior and can produce more aggressive compression depending on its truncation boundaries.

Experiments across several datasets and networks of different complexity show a competitive balance between efficiency and performance compared with other pruning methods. The contribution is both a theoretical basis for structured removal and a choice of pruning characteristics. The two versions offer different ways to balance compression against retained accuracy.
neurips-2024-bmrs-bayesian-model-reducti.tldr: BMRS uses Bayesian model reduction to prune whole network components, with two variants offering different compression behavior.

paragraphs: Serving several tasks with one language model becomes difficult when task-specific LoRA adapters are combined with quantization. The authors find that mainstream quantization methods obstruct sharing the base model across tasks. They also identify serving inefficiencies caused by limited support for adding tasks dynamically and by scheduling that overlooks differences between task workloads.

LoRA-Inlaid addresses both model storage and request scheduling. Its MLGPTQ quantization algorithm allows multiple adapters to share one quantized base model, reducing deployment memory. New adapters can be added while services remain online. A separate scheduling algorithm predicts output lengths and groups work across tasks, reducing memory use and frequent adapter switching.

The experiments report improvements over existing serving systems of up to 1.58 times for throughput, 1.76 times for average latency, two times for job completion time, and ten times for service-level-objective attainment, while retaining comparable model quality. These are reported maxima, not gains promised for every workload. Together, the results show the value of coordinating quantization and scheduling around the requirements of multiple adapters.
neurips-2024-efficient-multi-task-llm-qu.tldr: LoRA-Inlaid combines shared-model quantization and task-aware scheduling to serve multiple LoRA adapters more efficiently.

paragraphs: Jailbreaking attacks try to make language models produce harmful responses despite their safeguards. Many defenses rely on changing model weights or manually designed rules. This paper investigates whether optimizing an added prompt can provide an effective defense while preserving the model’s ability to answer ordinary requests.

Prompt Adversarial Tuning, or PAT, learns a control prompt that is attached as a guard prefix to the user’s prompt. Its optimization uses both adversarial inputs and benign requests. Including both kinds of input makes the training objective address attack resistance alongside normal task performance, rather than measuring defensive behavior in isolation.

The reported experiments cover grey-box and black-box attacks. PAT reduces the success rates of advanced attacks to nearly zero in those evaluations, preserves utility on the benign task, and adds negligible computational overhead. The result supports prompt optimization as a practical direction for language-model defense. The empirical scope matters: nearly zero success on the evaluated attacks does not establish that every future jailbreak will fail.
neurips-2024-fight-back-against-jailbrea.tldr: PAT learns a guard prefix from adversarial and benign prompts, sharply reducing evaluated jailbreak success while preserving ordinary task utility.

paragraphs: Safe reinforcement learning must balance useful behavior with limits on risk. This paper studies chance constraints, which express safety requirements probabilistically, rather than relying only on expected accumulated safety costs. It proposes a policy that chooses between two candidate actions using a potentially biased coin, with both candidates and the coin’s probability depending on the current state.

The authors establish a Bellman equation for chance-constrained decision processes and prove that an optimal policy of this flipping form exists. This is an existence result: it identifies a sufficient policy structure within the optimal solution set. Because joint chance constraints are difficult to solve directly, the paper also proves an approximation through expected cumulative safety constraints and establishes a corresponding optimal-policy existence result for that formulation.

For implementation, the authors adapt constrained policy optimization to train flipping policies and describe a framework applicable to other safe reinforcement learning algorithms. On Safety Gym benchmarks, flipping policies improve existing algorithms’ performance under the same safety-constraint limits. The practical contribution therefore connects a theoretical policy structure to measured gains in constrained control.
neurips-2024-flipping-based-policy-for-c.tldr: The paper proves that optimal chance-constrained policies can use state-dependent random choices between two actions and demonstrates practical performance gains.

paragraphs: Video frame interpolation creates frames between two existing images, making motion modeling central to the task. The authors argue that existing flow-based approaches do not sufficiently exploit useful motion information when combining flows or predicting them for specific times. Their method, Generalizable Implicit Motion Modeling, aims to represent how motion varies across both space and time.

GIMM first takes bidirectional flows from pretrained flow estimators and encodes them into a motion representation tailored to the input frames. An adaptive coordinate-based neural network then receives that representation together with spatial and temporal coordinates. This allows it to predict optical flow at arbitrary intermediate timestamps between the adjacent frames.

The method supplies motion estimates to existing flow-based interpolation systems, so its contribution can be incorporated into those pipelines. The authors report better performance than the current state of the art on standard interpolation benchmarks. The findings support the usefulness of encoding input-specific motion and querying it continuously in time, rather than relying solely on simpler flow combinations or isolated timestamp predictions.
neurips-2024-generalizable-implicit-moti.tldr: GIMM encodes motion between adjacent frames and predicts intermediate optical flows through a coordinate-based network, improving benchmark interpolation performance.

paragraphs: Gradients have complex relationships across many dimensions, making their probability distributions difficult to model. Accurate probability estimates are valuable for lossless compression, where the original values must be recoverable exactly. This paper investigates whether a large language model can supply such estimates for gradients in a zero-shot setting, with distributed learning as a motivating application.

The proposed LM-GC method combines a language model with arithmetic coding. It converts gradients into a text-like representation designed to preserve their structure while using symbols familiar to the language model. This conversion improves token efficiency by up to 38 times compared with plain representations, allowing the model to process gradient information more compactly.

Across the tested datasets and architectures, LM-GC improves compression rates by 10% to 17.2% over existing leading lossless methods. The authors also report promising compatibility with quantization and sparsification, which are themselves lossy techniques. Together, these findings suggest that language models can capture useful statistical regularities in numerical training data, extending their potential role beyond conventional text processing.
neurips-2024-language-models-as-zero-sho.tldr: LM-GC uses language-model probability estimates and arithmetic coding to improve lossless gradient compression without task-specific training.

paragraphs: Sharing a policy network helps multiple reinforcement learning agents learn efficiently, because they use fewer parameters and share experience. However, agents with shared parameters can develop overly similar behavior. Earlier approaches encourage diversity by linking agent identities to their trajectories, but the authors identify inefficient exploration when those methods have only limited trajectory visits to learn from.

Contrastive Trajectory Representation, or CTR, encourages diversity through learned representations of experience. An encoder and an autoregressive model map each agent’s trajectory into a latent space. Contrastive learning then makes these trajectory representations distinguishable through their relationships with learnable agent-identity representations, with an objective that maximizes mutual information between the two.

The authors implement CTR on top of QMIX and evaluate it on several cooperative multi-agent tasks. They report significant performance improvements over leading methods. The result supports learning distinguishable patterns of experience as a way to retain the efficiency of shared policies while encouraging agents to behave differently. Its demonstrated benefit is stronger cooperative performance in the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2024-learning-distinguishable-tr.tldr: CTR uses contrastive learning of trajectories and agent identities to encourage behavioral diversity and improve cooperative multi-agent performance.

paragraphs: Tumors contain many interacting tissue and cell types, and their contributions to prognosis can differ. Survival prediction from whole-slide images therefore involves more than recognizing cancerous regions in isolation. The paper argues that existing methods often overlook the differing prognostic roles of tissue types and the spatial relationships among them.

ProtoSurv addresses this with a heterogeneous graph model for survival prediction. Its learning process combines image-derived data with pathological knowledge. Specifically, the model accounts for tissue diversity, emphasizes prior knowledge about tissues related to prognosis, and represents spatial interactions across tissue types. These choices make biological distinctions part of the model’s representation rather than leaving learning entirely to undifferentiated image data.

The authors evaluate ProtoSurv on five cancer types from TCGA: BRCA, LGG, LUAD, COAD, and PAAD. They report performance superior to existing state-of-the-art methods in those evaluations. The findings support incorporating tissue-specific roles and spatial context into image-based survival modeling. The demonstrated contribution is improved prediction across these datasets, with tumor heterogeneity serving as useful modeling information.
neurips-2024-leveraging-tumor-heterogene.tldr: ProtoSurv combines tissue-aware graphs and pathological knowledge to improve whole-slide-image survival prediction across five evaluated cancer types.

paragraphs: Predicting a top-down map from a first-person image can provide a useful representation for ground robot navigation. However, models trained on autonomous-driving datasets may generalize poorly beyond the relatively small regions those datasets cover. This paper investigates whether public mapping platforms can supply a broader foundation for training map-prediction systems.

Map It Anywhere, or MIA, is a data engine that pairs Mapillary images with semantic maps from OpenStreetMap. The authors use it to automatically collect 1.2 million first-person and bird’s-eye-view pairs. The collection covers varied geographies, landscapes, environmental conditions, cameras, and capture scenarios. They then train a simple map-prediction model designed to work across camera models.

Evaluations on established benchmarks and the new dataset show that MIA data supports effective pretraining for generalizable map prediction. The authors report zero-shot performance exceeding baselines trained on existing datasets by 35%. The result highlights data scale and diversity as a promising route to broader geographic generalization, while the data engine makes those public resources usable for training and evaluation.
neurips-2024-map-it-anywhere-empowering-.tldr: MIA turns public street images and maps into large-scale training pairs that improve zero-shot bird’s-eye-view map prediction.

paragraphs: A language model can describe itself as an AI assistant without reliably using knowledge about itself or its circumstances. This paper makes that distinction measurable through the Situational Awareness Dataset, or SAD. It treats situational awareness as a collection of behavioral abilities assessed through question answering and instruction following.

SAD contains more than 13,000 questions across seven task categories. Tasks test whether models recognize their own generated text, predict their behavior, distinguish internal evaluations from real-world deployment, and follow instructions requiring self-knowledge. The authors evaluate 16 models, including pretrained base models and versions adapted for conversation.

All evaluated models score above chance, but even the highest-scoring model, Claude 3 Opus, remains far below a human baseline on certain tasks. General-knowledge performance only partly predicts SAD results. Chat models outperform their corresponding base models on SAD without the same advantage on general-knowledge tasks. These findings make self-related competence a distinct evaluation target, relevant to the benefits and safety risks of models capable of autonomous planning and action.
neurips-2024-me-myself-and-ai-the-situat.tldr: SAD measures language models’ behavioral knowledge of themselves and their circumstances, revealing abilities that general-knowledge scores only partly explain.

paragraphs: Memory-efficient language-model training can reduce optimizer storage by projecting it into a lower-dimensional subspace. Existing approaches often obtain the projection through singular value decomposition, but their convergence depends strongly on how that projection changes. This paper studies the theoretical consequences of updating the subspace during training.

The authors provide a convergence guarantee that accommodates arbitrary projection-matrix update rules within their analysis. It applies to optimizers that can be studied through Hamiltonian Descent, including common methods such as Adam and LION. Motivated by this result, they introduce Online Subspace Descent, which updates the projection using online principal component analysis instead of singular value decomposition and adds minimal training overhead.

The experiments pretrain LLaMA models ranging from 60 million to one billion parameters on C4. Across different tested settings, Online Subspace Descent achieves lower perplexity than leading low-rank training methods and moves closer to full-rank baselines. The findings connect a more flexible theoretical treatment of changing subspaces with a practical method for improving the quality of memory-efficient training.
neurips-2024-memory-efficient-llm-traini.tldr: Online Subspace Descent updates training subspaces with online PCA, backed by convergence analysis and improved low-rank language-model training results.

paragraphs: Demand-driven navigation asks an embodied agent to find objects that satisfy a person’s request. Earlier formulations typically assume one object is enough and do not account for individual preferences. This paper introduces MO-DDN, a benchmark in which satisfying a demand can require finding multiple objects while also considering personal preferences.

The authors address the expanded task with C2FAgent, a modular exploration method organized from coarse decisions to finer ones. It uses object attributes at different decision-making levels. Although attributes appeared in earlier demand-driven navigation work, this approach gives them roles within a modular exploration process rather than relying solely on attribute features in an end-to-end system.

Experiments show that the coarse-to-fine strategy outperforms the evaluated baselines. The authors attribute its benefit to making use of attributes at multiple levels of decision making. The paper’s contribution combines a more expressive task definition with an agent designed for that task, bringing evaluation closer to requests whose fulfillment involves several objects and differs between people.
neurips-2024-mo-ddn-a-coarse-to-fine-att.tldr: MO-DDN adds multiple objects and personal preferences to demand-driven navigation, while C2FAgent improves benchmark performance through coarse-to-fine attribute-based exploration.

paragraphs: Differential privacy protects information about individuals, but the mechanisms used to provide it can substantially reduce predictive performance. One way to reduce that cost is to prepare models using simulated data before learning from private records. This paper develops that idea into a meta-learning approach that learns how to construct a private predictor.

DPConvCNP combines a Convolutional Conditional Neural Process with an improved functional differential-privacy mechanism. Training on simulated data teaches the system to map private observations to a differentially private predictive model in a single forward pass. The objective includes producing accurate predictions with well-calibrated uncertainty, so the model’s confidence is part of the desired performance.

The authors compare DPConvCNP against a differentially private Gaussian process whose hyperparameters are carefully tuned. DPConvCNP performs better, particularly on non-Gaussian data, while requiring less tuning and running much faster at test time. The findings suggest that simulation-based meta-learning can help account for privacy-induced noise and make private regression both more accurate and easier to apply in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-noise-aware-differentially-.tldr: DPConvCNP learns from simulated data to build private regression predictors in one pass, outperforming a tuned private Gaussian-process baseline.

paragraphs: A single perplexity score on held-out text can conceal differences in how well a language model fits different kinds of language. Paloma addresses this by evaluating model fit across 546 English and code domains. Its premise is that performance on one distribution should not simply be assumed to carry over to others.

The benchmark includes two new datasets covering the top 100 subreddits and programming languages, drawing on sources common in language-model training. The authors also release six controlled one-billion-parameter baseline models. These controls support fair comparisons between pretraining corpora, and accompanying code lets other researchers apply the same experimental controls.

Case studies show what the finer breakdown reveals. Models trained only on Common Crawl data have unusual gaps in fit across many domains, and frequently occurring vocabulary strings dominate loss. These findings demonstrate why aggregate evaluation can hide consequential patterns. Paloma provides a way to examine where a model fits language well and how the composition of its training data relates to that fit.
neurips-2024-paloma-a-benchmark-for-eval.tldr: Paloma measures language-model fit across 546 domains, exposing patterns that a single aggregate perplexity score can conceal.

paragraphs: An agent may see only part of its environment during operation while having access to richer information, such as simulator states, during training. This paper analyzes when such privileged information makes reinforcement learning efficient. It focuses on practical training paradigms and separates the amount of experience needed from the computation required.

For teacher-student learning, the authors demonstrate a pitfall in obtaining near-optimal policies. They then identify a deterministic filter condition under which both sample and computational complexity are polynomial. For observable partially observable decision processes, they develop an asymmetric actor-critic algorithm with polynomial sample complexity and quasi-polynomial computational complexity. A key component learns belief states while preserving filter stability despite model misspecification.

The analysis also extends to multiple agents trained centrally but acting with decentralized information. Algorithms for both studied paradigms obtain polynomial sample complexity and polynomial or quasi-polynomial computation. These results clarify conditions under which privileged training information supports provably efficient learning, while avoiding computationally intractable oracles. They do not claim that richer training information automatically makes every partially observable problem easy.
neurips-2024-provable-partially-observab.tldr: The paper establishes conditional efficiency guarantees for practical partially observable reinforcement-learning methods that use privileged information during training.

paragraphs: Parameter-efficient finetuning usually adapts a large model by updating a small subset or addition of weights. This paper explores a different target for adaptation: the hidden representations that carry semantic information during computation. Representation Finetuning, or ReFT, keeps the base model frozen and learns task-specific interventions on those representations.

The authors introduce LoReFT, a version based on low-rank linear subspaces, along with a simpler variant that exchanges some performance for greater efficiency. Both are designed as drop-in alternatives to existing parameter-efficient methods. Their learned interventions are reported to be 15 to 65 times more parameter-efficient than LoRA.

Evaluations cover eight commonsense reasoning tasks, four arithmetic reasoning tasks, instruction tuning, and GLUE. Across these evaluations, the authors report the best balance of efficiency and performance, with ReFT methods almost always outperforming leading alternatives. The qualification matters: the claim is not a win on every comparison. The results support hidden representations as a useful place to apply compact learned adaptations without changing the underlying base model.
neurips-2024-reft-representation-finetun.tldr: ReFT adapts frozen language models through learned hidden-representation interventions, achieving strong task performance with substantially fewer parameters than LoRA.

paragraphs: Electronic health records frequently contain missing measurements, which can create misleading correlations and weaken patient-status predictions. Filling in every missing value is not necessarily helpful: difficult interpolation can introduce noise into the prediction process. SMART addresses this by making missingness part of representation learning rather than treating it solely as a problem of recovering raw values.

The method uses missing-aware attention across time and variables to encode information about absent observations. During self-supervised pretraining, it reconstructs representations of missing data in a latent space. This shifts reconstruction toward learned higher-order features instead of requiring the model to reproduce missing entries directly in the original input space.

The authors evaluate SMART on six electronic-health-record tasks and report better performance than state-of-the-art methods. They describe the attention mechanisms and representation-focused training as promoting generalization and robustness to missing data. The contribution is a coordinated way to encode missingness and learn from incomplete records, with improved predictive results in the evaluated tasks supporting that design.
neurips-2024-smart-towards-pre-trained-m.tldr: SMART models missingness explicitly and reconstructs latent representations during pretraining, improving patient-status prediction on six health-record tasks.

paragraphs: Forecasting several related time series involves a trade-off: treating channels independently can help resist distribution changes, but it ignores useful relationships between them. Modeling those relationships can become expensive or overly dependent on correlations that change. SOFTS is an MLP-based forecasting model designed to share information between channels efficiently.

Its central component, the STAR module, aggregates all series into a shared core representation. It then redistributes that core and combines it with each series’ own representation. This centralized exchange provides a route for channel interaction while aiming to reduce dependence on the quality of any individual channel. The shared core is the mechanism through which information moves among series.

The authors report performance above existing state-of-the-art methods with linear complexity. They also demonstrate experimentally that STAR can be used across different forecasting models. The results support a relatively simple way of incorporating cross-series information without the complexity of more distributed interaction mechanisms. The module’s demonstrated portability makes the contribution broader than a single forecasting architecture.
neurips-2024-softs-efficient-multivariat.tldr: SOFTS exchanges information among time series through a shared core, achieving strong forecasting results with linear complexity.

paragraphs: Automating suturing requires precise, adaptable manipulation, making realistic training environments important for reinforcement and imitation learning. The authors identify a gap in existing platforms: many emphasize relatively simple actions and offer too little flexibility for learning complex, decomposed tasks. SurgicAI provides a platform for developing and evaluating surgical policies around those requirements.

The platform supports modular suturing subtasks and their composition, allowing researchers to study both individual skills and task decomposition. It is compatible with the da Vinci Surgical System and provides a standardized process for collecting and using expert demonstrations. Multiple reinforcement-learning and imitation-learning approaches can be deployed through this shared infrastructure.

The authors implement and evaluate several algorithms on SurgicAI and provide explicit metrics and benchmarks for comparing learned policies. Their analysis highlights the platform’s potential to support progress in surgical robotics. The contribution is a common environment and evaluation pipeline for dexterous policy learning, making it possible to examine how methods handle individual subtasks and combinations within suturing scenarios.
neurips-2024-surgicai-a-hierarchical-pla.tldr: SurgicAI provides modular suturing environments, expert-demonstration workflows, and benchmarks for reinforcement and imitation learning in surgical robotics.

paragraphs: Evaluating generated video mainly for visual quality leaves important safety questions unanswered. Video also introduces risks involving events over time, which image-focused assessments do not fully address. T2VSafetyBench provides a structured benchmark for examining unsafe text-to-video outputs across four broad categories and 14 specific safety aspects.

The authors build a malicious-prompt dataset from real-world prompts, language-model-generated prompts, and jailbreak-based prompts. They then evaluate nine text-to-video models. This combination of a safety taxonomy and multiple prompt sources creates a common basis for comparing where models resist unsafe requests and where they remain vulnerable.

The evaluation finds that no model excels across every safety aspect. GPT-4 assessments generally correlate strongly with manual reviews, and the results reveal a trade-off between usability and safety. These findings argue for inspecting different dimensions of safety rather than treating model quality as one overall score. The benchmark is intended to support quantitative understanding of video-generation risks, including those that arise from temporal content.
neurips-2024-t2vsafetybench-evaluating-t.tldr: T2VSafetyBench evaluates nine video generators across 14 safety aspects, finding varied weaknesses and a usability–safety trade-off.

paragraphs: This paper studies how transformers learn to use patterns within their current input through a controlled sequence-modeling task. Each example comes from a Markov chain sampled from a prior distribution over chains. The setup lets the authors examine whether a model learns the transition statistics present in each context.

Training proceeds through several phases. Predictions are initially uniform, then begin using individual-token frequencies, or unigram statistics. A rapid transition later produces the correct solution based on adjacent-token, or bigram, statistics. The resulting statistical induction heads compute accurate next-token probabilities from those context-dependent bigram counts.

Empirical and theoretical analyses connect successful learning to interactions between transformer layers. The authors also find evidence that the easier unigram solution may delay the emergence of the better bigram solution. They vary the prior over Markov chains and consider extensions to longer token patterns. The study provides a concrete setting in which an intermediate strategy can be useful yet potentially slow the development of a more appropriate in-context computation.
neurips-2024-the-evolution-of-statistica.tldr: A controlled Markov-chain task reveals transformers progressing from token-frequency heuristics to accurate context-dependent transition modeling.

paragraphs: This paper asks how much training data full-batch gradient descent needs to generalize in non-smooth stochastic convex optimization. The distinction between fitting the observed sample and performing well on the underlying distribution is central. The analysis focuses on how dimension, sample size, learning rate, and iteration count jointly affect that distinction.

For common hyperparameter choices, the authors show that generalization error can scale as d/m + 1/√m, up to logarithmic factors, where d is dimension and m is sample size. This matches the sample complexity of worst-case empirical risk minimizers. In this setting, gradient descent therefore offers no better worst-case sample complexity than simply minimizing empirical risk.

A new bound also treats general hyperparameters. When dimension exceeds sample size, it establishes a necessary iteration count of order at least 1/ε⁴ to avoid overfitting at the target accuracy scale. This strengthens earlier lower bounds and resolves an open problem. The conclusions concern the specified non-smooth convex setting and expose how optimization choices interact with statistical generalization.
neurips-2024-the-sample-complexity-of-gr.tldr: In non-smooth stochastic convex optimization, full-batch gradient descent can match worst-case empirical risk minimizers’ sample complexity rather than improve it.

paragraphs: Training binary neural networks involves a combinatorial optimization problem. Common methods make gradient-based training possible through the straight-through estimator, but its theoretical basis remains limited. This paper introduces a framework grounded in Gaussian variational inference to better explain existing practices and develop a richer optimization approach.

In its simplest form, the framework produces a non-convex linear-programming formulation whose variables and gradients motivate latent weights and straight-through gradients. It also supports semidefinite-programming relaxations that explicitly model pairwise weight correlations. Those correlations provide a more detailed characterization of the training problem, but a direct formulation grows quadratically with the number of weights.

To address that scaling problem, the authors use the Burer–Monteiro approach and optimize low-rank solutions of linear size. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet show consistent improvements over the compared state-of-the-art binary-network training algorithms. The contribution links a theoretical account of familiar training tools with a practical way to incorporate weight correlations without retaining the full quadratic-size formulation.
neurips-2024-training-binary-neural-netw.tldr: A variational-inference framework motivates binary-network training heuristics and yields a low-rank optimization method that improves evaluated image-classification performance.

paragraphs: Many controlled systems evolve continuously, yet reinforcement learning often assumes decisions occur at fixed discrete intervals. Measurements and action changes can themselves be costly, especially when they require manual intervention. TaCoS addresses this by making the timing of interaction part of the learning problem, alongside the choice of control.

A TaCoS policy predicts both an action and how long to apply it. The authors formulate this as an extended Markov decision process that standard reinforcement-learning algorithms can solve. In experiments, leading algorithms trained with this formulation use substantially fewer interactions than their discrete-time counterparts while retaining or improving performance and remaining robust to changes in discretization frequency.

The paper also introduces OTaCoS, a model-based algorithm designed for this setting. For systems with sufficiently smooth dynamics, the authors prove sublinear regret, and experiments show further gains in sample efficiency. The smoothness condition is part of the theoretical result. Together, the methods show how learning when to observe and act can reduce interaction demands without sacrificing the evaluated control performance.
neurips-2024-when-to-sense-and-control-a.tldr: TaCoS learns both controls and their durations, reducing interactions, while OTaCoS adds sample-efficiency gains and a smoothness-dependent regret guarantee.
